note: Submodule of memory_limit_policy providing the 'role' MemoryLimitConstraint plugin (class Role). Cases are grounded in the real plugin id, its config keys, and its evaluate() logic. Medium/hard scripts use mlp_role_* policies built with the real 'role' constraint config and verified by loading the memory_limit_policy config entity.

evals.prompt: What is the constraint plugin id provided by the memory_limit_policy_role submodule, and what condition does it check on a request?
evals.expected_output: It registers the MemoryLimitConstraint plugin id 'role' (class Role). It matches when the current user has one of the configured roles.

evals.prompt: In a memory_limit_policy 'role' constraint, under which configuration key are the selected roles stored, and how are they matched?
evals.expected_output: Selected roles are stored under the 'roles' key (a map of role machine name => role machine name). evaluate() returns TRUE when the current user has ANY of those roles (array_intersect with current_user->getRoles()).

evals.prompt: Does a memory_limit_policy role constraint create any config dependencies, and what does the 'negate' option do to it?
evals.expected_output: Yes: calculateDependencies() adds a config dependency user.role.<id> for each selected role. Setting negate reverses the match (the policy then applies when the user does NOT have the selected role(s)).

evals.prompt: This Drupal site has an enabled memory limit policy 'mlp_role_known' whose only constraint is the 'role' condition from the memory_limit_policy_role submodule. Inspect the live configuration and report the value(s) configured for that constraint.
evals.expected_output: The policy mlp_role_known (config memory_limit_policy.memory_limit_policy.mlp_role_known) has a single 'role' constraint configured with authenticated. Read it from the entity's policy_constraints.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, create an enabled memory limit policy with machine id 'mlp_role_exec' (memory 768M) whose single constraint uses the 'role' condition from the memory_limit_policy_role submodule: a Role constraint that includes the 'authenticated' role. Apply it to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Create the memory_limit_policy config entity mlp_role_exec with memory '768M', status TRUE, and a policy_constraints entry {id: role, negate: false, ...} matching 'a Role constraint that includes the 'authenticated' role' (e.g. via the entity storage or the add-policy form).
